lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Practice using att-clauses to say what someone thinks or knows in everyday small talk.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Two colleagues have a short fika chat about the day and Swedish practice.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Sharing simple thoughts and confirming information.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik meet by the coffee machine and talk about how the day is going and why Swedish practice feels useful.

main_focus.name: att-clauses after thinking and knowing verbs
main_focus.description: Use att to connect a main clause with a simple idea or fact.
model_examples: Jag tror att mötet börjar klockan tio.
Jag vet att svenska är viktigt på jobbet.
Jag tycker att det är svårt men roligt.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use att-clauses naturally 3-4 times in the dialogue.

allowed_supporting_grammar: basic V2 word order in main clauses
basic modal verbs: kan, vill, ska, måste

vocabulary_target.theme: fika, workday thoughts, and Swedish practice
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Use several thought chunks, but keep the chat natural and light.

dialogue_shape.opening: One speaker starts a fika conversation and asks how the day feels.
dialogue_shape.middle: They share simple thoughts about work, Swedish, and the day using att-clauses.
dialogue_shape.ending: They finish with a positive or practical comment about continuing the day.

target_complexity.repetition: repeat the att-clause pattern enough for clear listening practice

focus: the situation/context of the fika conversation
the main opinion or thought about Swedish practice
the practical conclusion about the rest of the day

sentence_focus: one sentence with Jag tror att
one sentence with Jag vet att
one sentence with Jag tycker att
one sentence describing something as svårt or roligt
one fika sentence that includes an att-clause
